preconditions.description: The number of stations n, railways m, and queries q are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(w) == n and all(1 <= x <= 10**9 for x in w)
preconditions.description: The cost array w has exactly n elements, each being a positive integer within the specified range.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v and 1 <= d <= 10**9 for u, v, d in edges)
preconditions.description: Each railway connects two distinct stations with a positive integer length within bounds.
The number of railway definitions matches m.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= 4*10**8 for k, x in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query specifies a valid station index and a positive cost increment.
The number of queries matches q.
The initial graph of two-way railways is connected, allowing travel between any two stations.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q+1 lines, one for the initial state and one after each query.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(line, int) and line >= 0 for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is a non-negative integer representing the minimal cost.

Each output value represents the minimal total cost to construct one-way railways such that for every station v != 1, there exist at least two shortest paths from station 1 to v that are internally vertex-disjoint (share no stations except 1 and v), and the shortest path distance from 1 to v remains unchanged from the original graph.
